> ### ⚠ THE COUNT BELOW IS A LABEL COUNT, NOT AN EMITTABILITY PROOF
>
> `RE_EXPERIMENT_PROCESS_CORRECTIONS.md` §2: **"`emittable` additionally requires a complete
> generated recipe. Field labels alone are not an emittability proof."** The §8 promotion checker
> (`tools/agx-isa/promotion_check.py`), which opens the cited raw instead of trusting the citation,
> **blocks every emitter-grade row in the corpus, and 0 of the mnemonics counted below have all
> their rows clear.** The recipe dashboard reads **2 of 166 canonical-recipe-proven**.
>
> Read this file as what it is: a **sweep-ordering aid** — which field to attack next to move a
> descriptor along the *liveness* and *geometry* dashboards. It is NOT a completeness measure and
> must not be quoted as one. Run `python3 tools/agx-isa/dashboards.py` for the accounting, and
> `promotion_check.py` before believing any row is done.
>
> The promotion bar is now the five gates (A actual-byte ledger · B pre-registered
> detection-power control · C independent semantic predictor · D generated recipe with no donor ·
> E clean confirmation on a quiet machine), not the two-run agreement rule quoted below — which
> remains necessary but is no longer sufficient.

This file answers the question a dispatch actually needs: *which field do I sweep to move the next descriptor forward.* Ordered closest-first.

A field is emitter-grade only at `hardware-run` or `isolated-byte-diff` (`docs/evidence-classification.md`). Promotion requires two gated runs at **>=99%% per-value cross-run agreement AND movement >= 2x the disagreement count** — and a field that never moves is only promotable if the carriers differ **in the dimension the field controls**. Two carriers identical in that dimension are one carrier (EXP-0164; `iter_at.loc` read inert only because every carrier was `samples=1`).
